title: E-commerce Platform Report 2026
description: Ecommerce Platform Report 2026: how ecommerce technology is evolving, where merchants are spending, and what buyers should compare when selecting storefront platforms.
keyFindings: The ecommerce segment shows 22% year-over-year growth in 2026
Enterprise adoption of ecommerce solutions increased by 37% compared to last year
71% of organizations report improved outcomes after implementing ecommerce software
Small and medium businesses account for 52% of ecommerce software spending
AI-powered features are the top consideration for 56% of buyers evaluating ecommerce platforms
Cloud-based deployment represents 80% of new ecommerce software installations
Integration capabilities influence 72% of purchasing decisions
ecommerce software budgets increased by an average of 21% in 2026

sections.title: The Ecommerce Stack in 2026
sections.body: The ecommerce segment grew 22% year over year in our 2026 data. The category spans storefront platforms, headless commerce infrastructure, payments, and fulfillment tooling. Merchants increasingly combine a core storefront with specialized services for checkout, search, and personalization rather than buying everything from one vendor.

sections.title: Adoption Patterns
sections.body: Enterprise adoption of ecommerce solutions increased 37% compared to last year. The strongest growth is in platforms that scale from a single storefront to multi-channel operations with consistent product and inventory data. Teams also continue migrating from legacy on-premise systems to cloud storefronts as replacement cycles arrive.

sections.title: Spending Patterns
sections.body: Small and medium businesses account for 52% of ecommerce software spending, and budgets grew by an average of 21% in 2026. Pricing combines platform fees with transaction-based costs, so the effective cost depends on order volume and payment mix. Merchants should model total fees including payments and add-ons, not just the monthly plan.

sections.title: What Buyers Evaluate
sections.body: AI-powered features are the top consideration for 56% of buyers evaluating ecommerce platforms, including product recommendations, merchandising automation, and AI-assisted support. Integration capabilities influence 72% of purchasing decisions, with payments, shipping, and marketing automation connections ranking highest among merchant requirements.

sections.title: Regional Deployment Patterns
sections.body: Cloud-based deployment represents 80% of new ecommerce installations. Regional factors matter more in ecommerce than most categories: local payment methods, shipping carriers, and tax handling shape platform choices. Cross-border merchants favor platforms with multi-currency and multi-language capabilities built in.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.body: List the payments, tax, shipping, and marketing tools you depend on before comparing platforms, and confirm each has a maintained integration. Pilot the storefront on a subset of products, measuring conversion and site performance against the current baseline. Review the stack annually as transaction fees and AI features change the comparison.

methodology: This research is based on a survey of 2783 IT decision-makers, analysis of 103 software vendors, and secondary research from industry analysts. Data was collected in Q1-Q2 2026.
author: PilotStack Research Team
